=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (pairs of leaflets are clearly visible attached at the same node along the rachis)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): distal (leaflets are spaced out along the rachis, not clustered at the tip)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (the leaf is composed of multiple distinct leaflets attached to a central axis)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (there is a single terminal leaflet at the apex of the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 7 (one terminal leaflet and three pairs of lateral leaflets are visible on the primary leaf)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): opposite (the lateral leaflets are arranged in pairs at the nodes)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (the leaflet margins appear smooth and continuous)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): lanceolate (leaflets are longer than wide, tapering toward both ends)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (the leaflet tips come to a distinct, sharp point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate (the leaflets taper gradually into the petiolule)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (a central midrib is visible with secondary veins branching from it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible, fine, and numerous (secondary veins branch off the midrib at an acute angle and extend toward the margin)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny (the leaflets have a glossy, reflective surface texture)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no hairs or fuzz are visible on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): long (the petiole and rachis are elongated relative to the leaflet size)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (the rachis appears cylindrical and round in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (the young stems appear green and flexible rather than woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (the stems appear smooth and hairless)
    19. Stem color: green (the stems are a distinct green color)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (the stems appear uniform without ridges or prominent lenticels)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules are visible at the leaf bases)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex is visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus is visible at the leaf base)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: One leaflet shows a distinct notch or hole in the margin. The plant is growing at the base of a larger tree trunk.
